blocks.text: The three commands you will use most while developing: `gg run` (compile and run), `gg build` (produce a distributable executable) and `gg check` (type-check only, without generating code; the fastest).

code: gg run                      # debug mode: every run-time check on
gg build -o my_app          # a debug executable
gg check src/main.gg        # errors and warnings only

blocks.text: **Smart cache:** `gg build` keeps the SHA-256 hash of the source in `.gg-cache/`; if the code has not changed it says `Up to date (cached)` and does not rebuild. You can also build for other platforms with `--target` (`gg targets` lists which ones it can link).
For a detailed explanation of an error code there is `gg explain`; for the health of the machine and install there is `gg doctor`:

blocks.q: Which command shows only the errors, without generating code?
blocks.why: `gg check` type-checks and generates no code.

blocks.q: What does `gg build` do when the code has not changed?
blocks.why: The source's hash is compared with the cache.
